sights.address: 110 S Market St, San Jose, CA 95113
sights.w: Downtown's flagship art museum, set in a landmarked 1892 Richardsonian-Romanesque former post office joined to a modern wing, with a strong collection of modern and contemporary West Coast art.
sights.k: Closed Mondays; open Tue-Sun (Fri until 9pm). Paid admission.

sights.n: MACLA (Movimiento de Arte y Cultura Latino Americana)
sights.w: A contemporary arts space in the SoFA District grounded in the Chicano/Latino experience, showing visual art, performance, and spoken word with free admission.
sights.k: Gallery open Wed-Sun, roughly noon-5pm; free.

sights.n: San Jose Museum of Quilts & Textiles
sights.w: The first US museum devoted entirely to quilts and textiles, with rotating exhibitions of fiber art in the heart of the SoFA arts district.
sights.k: Open Thu-Sun; closed early week. Paid admission.

sights.n: Institute of Contemporary Art San Jose
sights.w: A non-collecting contemporary art center in SoFA showing rotating exhibitions by emerging and established artists, with free admission and an active public-programs schedule.
sights.k: Open Thu-Sun, noon-5pm; free.

sights.n: Peralta Adobe & Fallon House Historic Site
sights.address: 175 W St John St, San Jose, CA 95110
sights.w: Two eras side by side: the 1797 Peralta Adobe, the oldest surviving structure in San Jose and last remnant of the original Pueblo de San Jose, faces the ornate 1855 Fallon House built by an early city mayor.
sights.k: Interiors are seen by guided tour only, generally weekend afternoons, booked in advance; the site is run by History San Jose. The surrounding street was renamed Sharks Way near the arena.

sights.n: Japanese American Museum of San Jose
sights.w: In the heart of San Jose's Japantown, this museum collects and preserves Japanese American history and culture, including the WWII incarceration era, with a focus on the Bay Area.
sights.k: Open Thu-Sun, noon-4pm; closed Mon-Wed.

sights.n: Viet Museum (Museum of the Boat People & the Republic of Vietnam)
sights.w: Housed in the historic Greenwalt House within History Park at Kelley Park, this is believed to be the only museum focused on the Vietnamese diaspora and the boat-people exodus, in a city with one of the largest Vietnamese populations in the US.
sights.k: Limited hours (often weekends); confirm before visiting. Inside History Park at Kelley Park.

sights.address: 647 S King Rd, San Jose, CA 95116
sights.w: A 47-acre working farm park preserving San Jose's agricultural past, with the city's largest barn, a rare-fruit orchard, community gardens, and roaming farm animals, all free to visit.
sights.k: Open daily 8:30am to sunset; free.

sights.address: 399 W Taylor St, San Jose, CA 95110
sights.w: One of the largest public collections of rare and historic roses in the world, with roughly 3,000 varieties on nearly four acres of the Guadalupe River Park's Guadalupe Gardens.
sights.k: Open daily sunrise to sunset; free. Best bloom in spring.

sights.address: 170 S Market St, San Jose, CA 95113
sights.w: A 2.2-acre downtown park with a central fountain, ringed by the art museum, The Tech, and the adjacent Circle of Palms; on the site of the 1797 pueblo plaza, it is among the oldest public spaces in Northern California.
sights.k: Open daily; free. Hosts frequent festivals and Music in the Park.

sights.address: 1700 Alum Rock Ave, San Jose, CA 95116
sights.w: A landmark cultural campus on the Eastside, opened in 1999 and run by the School of Arts and Culture, with a 500-seat theater, galleries, gardens, and a pavilion celebrating Latino arts and heritage.
sights.k: Grounds and gardens are open to the public; indoor venues are event- and program-driven, so check the calendar.

sights.address: 1375 E Santa Clara St, San Jose, CA 95116
sights.w: The soaring Manueline-Gothic landmark of San Jose's Little Portugal, built 1916-19 partly from timbers salvaged from the Portuguese Pavilion of the 1915 Panama-Pacific Exposition.
sights.k: An active parish; visit respectfully and check Mass times before entering.

sights.w: The South First Area, downtown's compact arts-and-nightlife quarter along South First Street, packing MACLA, the ICA, the Quilts & Textiles museum, Anno Domini gallery, the historic California Theatre, and live-music venues into a few walkable blocks.
sights.k: A walkable district (representative address given). Liveliest on the free South First Fridays art walk, first Friday each month.

sights.address: Jackson St & N 5th St, San Jose, CA 95112
sights.w: One of only three surviving Japantowns in the United States and widely called the most authentic, this three-block Jackson Street district of family shops, markets, and restaurants dates to around 1900 and was named a California Cultural District in 2025.
sights.k: A walkable neighborhood (central intersection given). Pair with the Japanese American Museum on N 5th St.

sights.w: A tree-lined, small-town-feeling shopping and dining strip along Lincoln Avenue, with hundreds of independent boutiques, cafes, and restaurants a few miles southwest of downtown.
sights.k: A walkable district (central address given); pedestrian-friendly, best on foot.

sights.n: Don Edwards San Francisco Bay National Wildlife Refuge - Environmental Education Center
sights.w: The southern gateway to the first urban national wildlife refuge in the US, on the restored salt-pond wetlands at Alviso, with an education center, boardwalks, and miles of level trails prized for birdwatching.
sights.k: Trails open daily; the Environmental Education Center building keeps limited days/hours, so check ahead. Free.

sights.w: Stanford's free art museum, whose 24-hour outdoor Rodin Sculpture Garden holds some 20 monumental bronzes, one of the largest Rodin collections outside Paris, alongside wide-ranging galleries indoors.
sights.k: Museum closed Tue-Wed; free. The Rodin Sculpture Garden is open outdoors 24/7, free.

sights.w: A purpose-built museum next to the Cantor housing the Anderson family's gift of postwar American painting, with major works by Pollock, Rothko, de Kooning, and Diebenkorn, all free to see.
sights.k: Open Thu-Mon (closed Tue-Wed); free, no reservation needed.

sights.w: The 285-foot 1941 landmark tower at the center of Stanford's campus, home to the Hoover Institution's library and archives, with an observation deck that gives sweeping views over the Peninsula.
sights.k: The observation deck runs seasonal hours and closes for stretches (closed Aug 2026-Jan 2027); paid ticket to ascend. Verify it is open before visiting.

sights.w: A hands-on children's science museum paired with a small zoo of rescued and native animals, rebuilt and reopened in 2021 as a bright, interactive family destination.
sights.k: Closed Mondays; open Tue-Sun 10am-5pm.

sights.w: Palo Alto's beloved community donkeys graze a pasture beside the Bol Park bike path; one resident, Perry, was a live model for the Donkey character in Shrek.
sights.k: View free from the fence any time; volunteers host Sunday morning walks and feedings. Small pasture, not a formal attraction.

sights.w: A 1912 Mediterranean-Revival villa built by Senator James Phelan, now an arts center set in 175 hillside acres with formal gardens, an outdoor amphitheater, an artist residency, and free hiking trails through the redwoods.
sights.k: Grounds and trails open daily 8am-sunset, free parking on weekdays; villa interior access varies with events and tours.

sights.address: 106 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
sights.w: A community art and history museum in downtown Los Gatos with rotating contemporary-art and local-history exhibitions, an easy stop on a day trip to the town's shops and the Los Gatos Creek Trail.
sights.k: Closed Mon-Tue; open Wed-Sun. Free for Los Gatos residents and under-18s; modest admission otherwise.
